title: Forensic Log Model and SIEM Export Playbook (v0.1)
content:
Overview:
This playbook is a working draft that defines a forensic-first audit log model and recommended SIEM export mechanics for RBAC v2 and evidence automation. Purpose is to: (1) produce a single, exportable NDJSON-compatible event model suitable for long-term retention and SIEM ingestion; (2) define mapping and transformation rules to preserve backwards compatibility with v1/v2/v3 audit payloads; (3) outline hooks for automated evidence bundles (signed snapshots, KMS references) that can be consumed by compliance teams and incident response; (4) provide operational guidance for export throughput, partitioning, and retention tiers.

Intended audience:
- Security & compliance engineers
- Observability/telemetry owners
- SRE/Platform teams responsible for SIEM exports and retention policies
- Solutions/Support teams onboarding enterprise customers that require attestations or eDiscovery

Scope and non-scope:
- IN SCOPE: API audit events, admin console actions, model-serving critical events (deploy, rollback, model-version-change), access/grant/revoke RBAC-v2 actions, evidence bundle generation events, export records to SIEM
- OUT OF SCOPE: high-volume application-level telemetry (application logs), low-fidelity analytics events that are not relevant to compliance

Design goals / constraints:
- Forensic fidelity: every exported record must include stable identifiers (request_id, trace_id) and principal attributes as-of-event (actor_id, actor_role, auth_method) to reduce reliance on external lookup services for investigations.
- Backward compatibility: provide deterministic transformations from existing v1..v3 payloads so historical archives remain queryable.
- SIEM-friendly: prefer NDJSON with flattened top-level fields and a small number of well-known nested maps (metadata, resource).
- Privacy-aware: PII minimization by default; full attributes gated behind enterprise contracts and RBAC.

Primary event taxonomy (for forensics):
- auth: login, token-create, token-revoke, session-expire, failed-auth
- access_control: grant, revoke, role-assignment-change, policy-edit, rbac-v2-role-create
- config_change: infra-config-update, model-deploy, model-rollback, route-change
- data_access: secrets-read, dataset-download, artifact-access
- inference_ops: request-create, request-complete, request-timeout, cache-hit, cache-evict
- system: node-start, node-stop, capacity-breach, autoscale-event
- evidence: evidence-bundle-created, evidence-bundle-signed, evidence-requested
- export: siem-export-success, siem-export-fail, export-backfill-start/complete

Canonical field glossary (flattened top-level recommended):
- ts: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp string (e.g. 2024-11-15T13:22:05Z)
- event_id: stable UUID v4
- event_type: one of taxonomy values (see above)
- severity: info|warning|error|critical
- actor_id: stable principal identifier (user:alice@acme.com or service:ingest-worker)
- actor_role: role snapshot string (e.g. platform-admin, org-security-readonly) -- from RBAC v2 role snapshot at event time
- auth_method: oauth|service-token|sso|mfa|api-key
- action: free-text short verb (create, update, delete, read, start, stop, sign)
- resource_type: model|project|dataset|secret|route|pool|deployment
- resource_id: stable resource identifier (project:acme/prod or model:rw-7B:2024-10-23)
- outcome: success|failure|partial|denied
- request_id: request-scoped id (propagated across services)
- trace_id: distributed trace id (if present)
- latency_ms: integer or null for non-request events
- tokens_in: integer (for inference requests)
- tokens_out: integer (for inference requests)
- model_version: string (if applicable)
- model_variant: string (quantization/compile profile snapshot)
- kv_cache_hit: true|false|null
- evidence_bundle_id: id referencing an archived evidence bundle (if event produced evidence)
- retention_tier: hot|warm|cold|archive (used by export/retention job)
- raw_payload: optional base64-encoded blob for high-fidelity capture (access controlled)

Example NDJSON event (single-line):
{"ts":"2024-11-15T13:22:05Z","event_id":"2b7f9e94-1a6c-4d3b-9f88-0f3a7e2d7c8a","event_type":"inference_ops","severity":"info","actor_id":"service:frontend-1","actor_role":"ingest-worker","auth_method":"service-token","action":"request-create","resource_type":"model","resource_id":"model:rw-7B:2024-10-23","outcome":"success","request_id":"req-12345","trace_id":"trace-98765","latency_ms":45,"tokens_in":12,"tokens_out":80,"model_version":"rw-7B-2024-10-23-1","model_variant":"q4_0","kv_cache_hit":false,"retention_tier":"hot"}

Backwards compatibility mapping (v1..v3 -> v0.1 canonical):
- v1 had user_email and action_label; map user_email -> actor_id (prefix user:), map action_label -> action.
- v2 introduced nested 'actor' object; flatten to actor_id and actor_role.
- v3 added model telemetry fields under inference_metrics; map tokens and latency into top-level tokens_in/tokens_out/latency_ms.
- Migration rule: export a companion _legacy_meta field for any event that had non-mappable structured payload to preserve raw context.

SIEM export mechanics and formats:
- Primary export format: NDJSON (one event per line) with gzip rotation.
- Secondary: CEF/LEEF mapping layer for customers who require older formats (implement mapping table).
- Delivery modes: push (syslog/TCP) for enterprise SIEMs, S3 raft files for cloud SIEM ingestion, and direct Elastic ingestion via bulk API for Redwood-managed observability.
- Partitioning: partition by day and retention_tier. For large customers (>5TB/mo) partition further by project_id.
- Ordering: do not rely on write-order for completeness; use event_id + ts for deduplication and reassembly.

Operational sizing notes (rough):
- Average event size (canonical NDJSON): ~800 bytes
- Estimate: 10M events/day -> ~8GB/day of NDJSON compressed to ~2.5–3GB (gzip).
- SIEM backfill capability: bulk backfill jobs should accept compressed multi-day bundles and record backfill manifest events: export-backfill-start/complete with evidence_bundle_id.

Evidence automation hooks and content:
- When an evidence-generating event occurs (e.g., policy-change, admin-sensitive-action), create an evidence bundle: signed archive containing full event stream slice + related artifacts (config snapshots, cluster topology, relevant traces, KMS-wrapped keys).
- Evidence bundle metadata fields: evidence_bundle_id, created_by, created_at, signature_kid, kms_key_ref, retention_policy, accessible_via_link (timebound).
- Signed attestations: support CMS-style signature (detached) and SHA256 manifest. Record evidence-bundle-signed events with signature_kid and storage_location.
- Access controls: evidence retrieval requires enhanced auth (`evidence:read`) and VPC path restrictions for private deployments.

RBAC v2 integration notes (how to capture role snapshot):
- At any security-relevant event we must capture the actor_role snapshot. This can be either: (a) embed the role snapshot into the event at emit-time, or (b) include a role_snapshot_ref with an append-only role snapshot store referenced by role_snapshot_id. Prefer (a) for forensic immutability; (b) can be used to reduce payload sizes when policy is very stable.
- Admin bypass actions must be flagged with admin_override=true and include justification_id if provided by the operator UI.

Export reliability and retries:
- Export worker must persist export manifest and offsets. On transient failure attempt exponential backoff up to 24 hours and generate export-failure events with reason codes.
- Heartbeat events every 1 minute to SIEM export topic to surface liveness and lag metrics.

Migration and rollout plan (high-level):
1) Finalize canonical field glossary and publish transformation library (python + go) that converts v1..v3->v0.1. (owner: Arjun)
2) Implement NDJSON exporter in export pipeline; add config knobs for partitioning and retention_tier. (owner: Leah)
3) Add evidence bundle generator prototype behind feature flag; integrate with KMS for signing. (owner: Sofia)
4) Pilot with 2 internal teams for 4 weeks (observability + solutions).
5) Gradual opt-in rollout for enterprise tenants; provide backfill tooling and mapping docs.

Open questions / risks:
- How much of the actor_role snapshot do we include to avoid leaking PII? (role names can include org info)
- Should raw_payload be enabled by default for Hosted customers? (privacy risk)
- How to reconcile cross-region exports and multi-cloud SIEM endpoints (latency, ordering)?
- Legal/eDiscovery: retention tiers and e-discovery holds need integration with legal workflow (who signs off on evidence deletion?).

Immediate TODOs (next 2 weeks):
- Create transformation library repo and seed with v1->v0.1 mapping (SEC-2345). (Arjun)
- Prototype NDJSON export + S3 sink and test gzipped rotation. (Leah)
- Draft Confluence page that becomes the canonical schema reference and include this playbook as a subpage. (Maya)

References and artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Audit+Schema+Home
- Jira: SEC-2345 (schema transformation), SEC-2370 (evidence-bundles), SEC-2401 (siem-export-pipeline)
- Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/842 (exporter prototype)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally pragmatic and forensic-first; feedback welcome on fields that feel redundant or missing.
- If you need to run queries for early pilot, export the sample ndjson and ingest into a local Elastic snapshot to validate mappings.

Author notes / voice-of-draft:
- Portions of this doc were pulled together quickly during on-call and follow-up with the observability team — expect some shorthand and TODOs.
- I intentionally prefer explicit snapshotting of role and model variant to simplify future investigations; we can optimize payload size later with a role_snapshot_ref approach if volume becomes an issue.

-- end of draft v0.1 --
